title: Heisenberg-Scaling Quantum Metrology of Electron-Photon Coupling via Multi-Electron PINEM
authors: Zihang Zou, Feng-Xiao Sun, Yunquan Liu, Qiongyi He
abstract: Free-electron quantum optics has recently emerged as a promising platform for coherent electron-light interactions, yet its potential for quantum-enhanced metrology remains largely unexplored. Here, we investigate the fundamental precision limit of coupling-strength estimation in multi-electron photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), demonstrating that the quantum Fisher information scales quadratically with electron number. We then propose an experimentally accessible scheme combining squeezed-light probing and optical homodyne detection that attains Heisenberg scaling with respect to electron number, provided the electrons exhibit nonzero inter-electron coherence, while surpassing conventional PINEM sensing in photon-number enhancement as well. We further analyze the effect of imperfect electron preparation, showing that electron phase noise is converted into a fluctuating optical displacement and eventually limits the precision. To overcome this limitation, an auxiliary optical mode coupled to the same electron ensemble measures the displacement noise in the signal mode, allowing its conditional suppression and recovery of the Heisenberg scaling. Our work establishes multi-electron coherence as a resource for free-electron quantum metrology and opens the route to precision measurements of nanoscale electron-light interactions.
summary: The paper investigates quantum-enhanced metrology for measuring electron-photon coupling in multi-electron PINEM. It demonstrates that by utilizing squeezed light and an auxiliary measurement mode, the estimation precision can reach the Heisenberg limit scaling with electron number. This establishes multi-electron coherence as a key resource for high-precision nanoscale measurements.
main_problem: To determine the fundamental precision limit for estimating the electron-photon coupling strength in multi-electron near-field electron microscopy (PINEM) and achieve quantum-enhanced metrology.
main_result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling ($\propto N_e^2$) in the estimation precision, surpassing conventional sensing limits, and this scaling can be recovered even with imperfect electron preparation using an auxiliary optical mode.
method: The analysis uses the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) derived from the system's unitary evolution operator, employing squeezed-light probing and homodyne detection in conjunction with conditional measurements.
model_or_system: The system involves multi-electron quantum optics interacting with an optical field via a PINEM interaction Hamiltonian. The platform utilizes an electron ensemble and incorporates concepts from quantum estimation theory.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), estimation sensitivity ($\chi^{-2}$), quadrature variance ($\Delta^2 X_s$), and the coupling strength $g_s$.
important_parameters: Electron number ($N_e$), average photon number ($N_{ph}$), squeezing parameter ($r$), and the degree of inter-electron coherence.
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes ideal comb states or utilizes Gaussian approximations for the electron phase distribution; the recovery mechanism relies on the auxiliary mode acting as a syndrome channel.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the experimental apparatus, compare the scaling of sensitivity ($\chi^{-2}$) for conventional versus proposed schemes against $N_{ph}$, and show the recovery of ideal scaling using an auxiliary mode.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the QFI limit for the multi-electron system, then proposing an experimentally accessible scheme using squeezed light, analyzing the degradation due to phase noise, and finally introducing an auxiliary mode and conditional measurements to recover the optimal Heisenberg scaling.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses quantum metrology in a complex, open quantum system involving light-matter interaction at the nanoscale, providing concrete pathways to surpass the standard quantum limit using collective quantum resources.

A train of Ne electrons emitted from an electron gun is prepared in identical coherent comb states by cascaded interactions with classical light fields and free-space propaga- tion (FSP) with the method developed in Ref. [52]. The pre- pared electrons subsequently interact, through the PINEM coupling gs, with two orthogonally squeezed states, S(r)|0⟩ and S(−r)|0⟩. Homodyne detection is applied to the output modes therefore provides independent estimates the real and imaginary parts of the coupling strength gs.

(a) Dependence on the electron number Ne at a fixed phase- distribution width σ = 0.5. (b) Dependence on σ at a fixed electron number Ne = 20. The accumulated phase fluctua- tions introduce a classical noise contribution that grows with Ne and with σ, destroying the ideal χ−2 ∝N 2 e scaling and reducing the metrological advantage.
